Trying to Conceive

Coming Off Birth Control: What to Expect

Updated: July 1, 2026

This article is shown in English while its translation is prepared.

Deciding to stop contraception is an exciting step. How quickly your fertility and cycles return depends on the method you were using — here is what to expect so there are no surprises.

Fertility usually returns quickly

For most methods, fertility returns soon after stopping. With the combined pill, mini-pill, patch, ring, implant, or hormonal and copper IUDs, it is possible to conceive within the first cycle after stopping or removal.

You do not need a "washout" period for most methods, though giving yourself a cycle or two to track your natural rhythm can be helpful.

The one exception: the injection

The contraceptive injection is the notable exception. After stopping it, it can take several months — sometimes up to a year — for ovulation and fertility to fully return.

If you are planning ahead and using the injection, it is worth stopping well before you want to conceive.

What your cycles may do

After hormonal contraception, your natural cycle may take a little time to settle into its own pattern. The first few periods can be irregular, and that is usually normal.

Tracking your cycle from the start helps you learn your fertile window and spot when things have settled.

Get ready while you transition

Start (or continue) a prenatal vitamin with folic acid as soon as you begin trying, and ideally before. Adopt fertility-friendly habits for both partners.

If your periods have not returned after a few months (longer for the injection), or were irregular before contraception, check in with your provider.

Key takeaways

  • For most methods, fertility can return within the first cycle after stopping.
  • The contraceptive injection is the exception — return can take months.
  • Early cycles off hormonal birth control may be irregular; that is normal.
  • Start a folic-acid prenatal as soon as you begin trying.
  • See a provider if periods do not return after a few months.

Frequently asked questions

Can I get pregnant right after stopping the pill?

Yes. Fertility can return in the first cycle after stopping the pill, so use another method until you are ready to conceive.

Do I need to wait a few months after stopping the pill?

Medically there is no required wait for most methods. Some people take a cycle or two simply to track their natural rhythm, but it is a personal choice.

Why is the injection different?

Its hormones linger longer, so ovulation and fertility can take several months to return after the last dose.

This article is general education, not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always talk with a qualified healthcare professional about your situation, and seek urgent care for emergencies.
